newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes steady in Asia, no firm bid heard for Minas.
newsitem.headline: Crudes steady in Asia, no firm bid heard for Minas.

text.p: Crude oil prices stayed mostly stable in late Asia on Friday, with buying interest seen for Minas but no firm bids emerging for the crude, traders said.

Some traders said they were closely following U.N. Security Council deliberations on whether an Iraqi pilgrim flight to Saudi Arabia violated sanctions imposed on Baghdad for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. Their concern was that the outcome of the discussion could affect Iraqi crude oil exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.
At 0800 GMT June cash Brent was assessed at $18.10/18.20 a barrel.
On SIMEX, the June Brent contract was bid/offered at $18.14/18.22 in afternoon trading compared with the contract's settlement of $18.14 on London's IPE on Thursday.
In spreads, June Brent/Dubai was assessed at $1.35/1.45 after a trade was done at $1.45 between a trader and a European oil company.
In the physical market for regional crudes, China was showing an interest in buying Minas but no firm bids appeared to be indicated, traders said.
May Minas was offered at a premium of about ICP plus five cents, they said.

In Gulf crudes, Petron was widely believed to have purchased 500,000 barrels of Qatar Marine in its tender which closed on Monday. The name of the seller was not immediately available. Traders were uncertain of the level at which the deal was done, but it was generally believed to have been done at Dubai quotes plus 75 to 80 cents.

In other Gulf crude trades, a June Masila was believed to have been exchanged between a trader and a South Korean refining company. The deal was believed to have been done at a five-cent premium to the official selling price.
